# Problem 1

```{r, summarize}
data("ny_noaa")
ny_noaa

ny_noaa |>
  summarize(
    n_stations = n_distinct(id),
    first_date = min(date),
    last_date = max(date)
  )

ny_noaa |>
  summarize(
    missing_prcp = sum(is.na(prcp)),
    missing_snow = sum(is.na(snow)),
    missing_snwd = sum(is.na(snwd)),
    missing_tmax = sum(is.na(tmax)),
    missing_tmin = sum(is.na(tmin))
  )

```

The NY NOAA dataset contains 2,595,176 daily observations from 747 weather stations, spanning January 1, 1981, through December 31, 2010. The seven variables include station ID, date, precipitation, snowfall, snow depth, and maximum and minimum temperatures. Missing data are common, particularly for temperature. Overall, 5.6% of precipitation, 14.7% of snowfall, 22.8% of snow depth, and 43.7% of maximum and minimum temperature observations are missing.


```{r, clean data}
noaa_df =
  ny_noaa |>
  separate(
    date,
    into = c("year", "month", "day"),
    sep = "-"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    tmax = as.numeric(tmax) / 10,
    tmin = as.numeric(tmin) / 10,
    prcp = prcp / 10
  )

```

## Snow Fall
```{r, snow}
noaa_df |>
  count(snow, sort = TRUE)
```
The most commonly observed snowfall value is 0 mm, reflecting that most days have no snowfall. The most frequent positive values are 25, 13, and 51 mm. These are approximately equivalent to 1, 0.5, and 2 inches, suggesting that measurements were originally recorded in rounded inch increments and then converted to millimeters.

## Temperature
```{r, temp}
temperature_df =
  noaa_df |>
  filter(month %in% c("01", "07")) |>
  group_by(id, year, month) |>
  summarize(
    mean_tmax = mean(tmax, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  drop_na(mean_tmax)

temperature_df |>
  mutate(
    year = as.numeric(year),
    month = factor(
      month,
      levels = c("01", "07"),
      labels = c("January", "July")
    )
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = mean_tmax, group = id)) +
  geom_line(alpha = .2) +
  facet_grid(~ month) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(1981, 1990, 2000, 2010)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Average maximum temperature by station",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Average maximum temperature (°C)"
  )

temperature_df |>
  filter(month == "07", mean_tmax < 15)

noaa_df |>
  filter(id == "USC00308962", year == "1988", month == "07") |>
  drop_na(tmax) |>
  summarize(
    observed_days = n(),
    mean_tmax = mean(tmax),
    min_tmax = min(tmax),
    max_tmax = max(tmax)
  )

```

The average maximum temperatures are consistently higher in July than in January. January shows greater variation between years, while stations generally follow similar annual patterns within each month. One notable outlier is station USC00308962 in July 1988, which had an average maximum temperature of 14C. This does not appear to be due to missingness, as all 31 days had reported maximum temperatures, ranging from 8.3C to 20.6C. Further investigation would be needed to determine whether this reflects actual weather conditions or a recording issue.

## Temperature Maximum/Minimum Plots
```{r, plots, fig.width=10, fig.asp=.5}
temperature_plot =
  noaa_df |>
  drop_na(tmin, tmax) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = tmin, y = tmax)) +
  geom_bin2d() +
  scale_fill_continuous(
    breaks = c(20000, 60000),
    labels = c("20,000", "60,000")
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Daily Max/Min Temperature",
    x = "Minimum temperature (°C)",
    y = "Maximum temperature (°C)",
    fill = "Count"
  )

snowfall_plot =
  noaa_df |>
  filter(snow > 0, snow < 100) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = snow)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  scale_x_discrete(
    breaks = c("1981", "1990", "2000", "2010")
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Snowfall by year",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Snowfall (mm)"
  )

temperature_plot + snowfall_plot
```
```

Daily maximum and minimum temperatures show a strong positive relationship, with some isolated potential outliers away from the main cluster. Among snowfall observations greater than 0 and less than 100 mm, distributions are fairly similar across years, with medians around 25 mm and right-skewed distributions. Potential snowfall outliers appear in the early 2000s - 2010, with values roughly between 80 and 100 mm. Overall, the typical snowfall amount appears relatively stable across years.
